title: A navigation's current entry index can be −1 even when it does not have entries and events disabled
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

Currently, when [getting the current entry of a navigation](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#navigation-current-entry), the spec checks if the [navigation has entries and events disabled](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#has-entries-and-events-disabled), and if not, asserts that the [navigation's current entry index is not −1](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#navigation-api-core:navigation-current-entry-index).

However, in the case of an iframe whose [document is initial about:blank](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#is-initial-about:blank) and then has [`document.open()`](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-document-open) called on it, we end up in a state where [the document is no longer initial about:blank](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#opening-the-input-stream:is-initial-about:blank) but the navigation's current entry index is still -1. If a fragment navigation (or an additional `document.open`) is then attempted within this iframe, we will end up within the [update the navigation API entries for a same-document navigation](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#update-the-navigation-api-entries-for-a-same-document-navigation) steps with `has entries and events disabled` being false, and so when we enter [step 2](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#navigation-api-entry-updates:navigation-current-entry) we will trigger the aforementioned assertion.

This came up when looking at failures of a Gecko-internal test (https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/source/dom/html/test/test_bug478251.html, https://treeherder.mozilla.org/logviewer?job_id=531454468&repo=try&task=aSvFFj98Qe6v4MAU9FDvTw.0&lineNumber=3981). It appears that this specific failure does not occur within Blink or Webkit as they treat document's which have had `document.open` called on them as being in a form of intermediate state of `initial about:blank`, which they still consider as having entries and events disabled (see https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/core/loader/frame_loader.h;l=337;drc=c5fe0d8a9bd7720d7c8738130a24ac7597178c87 and https://searchfox.org/wubkat/rev/919691a4ebb09a93c2dc093686cdc284e35ff623/Source/WebCore/loader/FrameLoaderStateMachine.h#48).
